ideaReviews.summary: Strong fit: Amsterdice on 29 Nov (€10 with two coins), OBA Bordspellencafé on 28 Nov (fee unstated, solo visitors explicitly welcome), plus four dated Wednesday game nights at Roode Remise marked free.
ideaReviews.nextStep: Prefer OBA for lower cost/clear solo access; Amsterdice for a larger day event.

ideaReviews.summary: Amsterdam Chess Meetup at Café de Laurierboom on 14 Nov, 11:00–13:00, is explicitly free and all levels are welcome.
ideaReviews.nextStep: Attend as a low-cost, short daytime social session; skill level need not be established.

ideaReviews.summary: Two date-specific beginner-friendly RPG options surfaced: Netherlands Roleplaying Guild 14 Nov (free, 18+, first-time-player games; 13:00–18:00) and D&D Amsterdam 21 Nov (free, 18+, RSVP, beginner help; 13:00–18:30).
ideaReviews.nextStep: Check which game tables and places remain before choosing.

ideaReviews.summary: No dated pub quiz with a clearly stated solo-player joining policy was verified in this research batch.
ideaReviews.nextStep: Keep as a lead only; search venue calendars rather than assuming solo team assignment.

ideaReviews.summary: Four already-listed November repair cafés now have an explicit local price policy: free admission and repair help, optional contribution, parts/refreshments may cost extra.
ideaReviews.nextStep: Choose based on date and venue fit; confirm whether the specific item can be repaired.

ideaReviews.summary: No separately dated visible-mending circle was verified here. OBA’s sewing atelier is already present as an undated event lead in the main inventory; its one-off November date and entry cost remain unconfirmed.
ideaReviews.nextStep: Check OBA calendar for a dated drop-in before treating this as available.

ideaReviews.summary: Serve the City’s current calendar has dated kitchen/serving volunteering shifts through November; these are volunteer roles rather than public meals. Current event pages did not establish a fee or open capacity.
ideaReviews.nextStep: Check the specific shift details and sign-up availability; do not assume meal participation or zero cost.

ideaReviews.summary: The existing Serve the City November Action Day includes a dated Boterbloem self-harvest garden shift; the STC calendar calls it volunteering, not a general public garden drop-in.
ideaReviews.nextStep: Use the existing Nov 14 event record and verify open capacity.

ideaReviews.summary: The existing STC green-volunteering agenda lists dated November park cleanups; each is a signup-based group activity.
ideaReviews.nextStep: Use the existing Nov 7 or Nov 14 records; suitability depends on travel to the park and remaining places.

ideaReviews.summary: Existing IVN Amsterdam event records provide dated nature walks in October and November. KNNV’s Diemerbos photo walk is also dated 20 Nov but membership access is unclear.
ideaReviews.nextStep: Prefer IVN’s public dated walks if non-member access is important.

ideaReviews.summary: No dated public citizen-science observation session was verified in this batch.

KNNV’s Diemerbos photography walk is dated for 20 Nov, 10:00, but is described as a KNNV member working group and non-member eligibility is unclear. A separate 14 Nov analogue photowalk at Cameranu was sold out when checked.
ideaReviews.nextStep: Confirm KNNV membership access before recommending; do not list the sold-out Cameranu photowalk as available.

ideaReviews.summary: Amsterdam Book Club has two 15 Nov sessions in English at Café Conrad (€10 including one drink); its organizer says many attendees come alone. Reading The Bell Jar beforehand is expected.
ideaReviews.nextStep: Choose a session only if the book preparation and RSVP fee suit.

ideaReviews.summary: Socrates Café has individually listed Sunday OBA discussions throughout November, 15:00–17:00, free. The organizer requires basic spoken English but says listening without speaking is fine.
ideaReviews.nextStep: Best discussion option if English and a structured philosophical conversation appeal.

ideaReviews.summary: A free, audience-welcome jazz jam is listed at BIMHUIS on 24 Nov 22:00–00:30. It is a live music jam, not a facilitated body-percussion or vocal-improvisation workshop.
ideaReviews.nextStep: Use as a music/social evening if the late finish suits; performer sign-up details are not stated.

findings: Best centrally located low-cost social options found in this batch: OBA Roelof Hartplein board games on 28 Nov (solo-friendly, fee unstated), Socrates Café at OBA Oosterdok on five Sundays in November (free; English participation required), and Café de Laurierboom chess on 14 Nov (free, all levels).
For a structured first-time activity, the Netherlands Roleplaying Guild on 14 Nov and D&D Amsterdam on 21 Nov are both free, adult-only (18+) and explicitly support first-timers.
Amsterdice is farther east but offers a large all-day board-game event on 29 Nov; organizers explicitly say people attend alone and the €10 fee includes two coins.
Repair-café fee policy can now be stated from the local Amsterdam organizer: free entry and help, optional donation, replacement parts/refreshments may cost extra.
BIMHUIS Tuesday Jam on 24 Nov is free, reservation-free, and welcomes musicians of all ages and levels plus jazz listeners; the 00:30 finish is late.
gaps: No explicit fee or language appeared on OBA Bordspellencafé page.
No dated public pub quiz with a solo-team policy was verified.
No dated citizen-science event or separate mending circle was verified.
KNNV photo-walk access for non-members remains unclear.
Event capacity is live and can change after 18 Oct; availability is not guaranteed by this snapshot.

The official Amsterdam municipal site returned an automated block during direct browsing; its page content was still available through previously captured municipal listing/search results, so no additional city-calendar instances were added here.
MAQAM lists MAJAM November for 12 Nov 2026 as free, but the linked event detail page still displays a 2025 date; excluded pending a corrected event page.
